body:
STOP — BUG-1495 IS NOW BLOCKED ON A SPEC THAT CANNOT MERGE. The dependency is right; the target is wrong. It should point at BUG-1445, and if it does, BUG-1495 is unblocked right now rather than parked.

BUG-1476 is `done`, not superseded — my supersede recommendation from this afternoon has not been actioned, so it is still sitting there looking like a live dependency. It is not:

  - Its PR #2029 carries a SEMANTIC conflict that cannot be resolved as-is. Both sides implement
    the same function — main's `blocking_rework_verdict` (trace:BUG-1445) and the branch's
    `rework_guard_verdict` (trace:BUG-1476). Resolving it means giving an existing function a
    second name.
  - Its production fix is redundant. BUG-1445 is `completed`, merged as #2028, and I verified
    the guard is in the RUNNING binary (wave b09197ab72), not merely on main.

So `BUG-1495 BlockedBy BUG-1476` parks BUG-1495 behind a PR nobody can land, waiting for a fix that shipped three hours ago under a different spec id.

THE REVIEWER'S CHAIN IS CORRECT AND IT ARGUES FOR THE OPPOSITE CONCLUSION. Their evidence — BUG-1297's branch carrying one commit from 08:02 while two later runs produced nothing in 50s and 14s — is exactly BUG-1476's thesis. But that thesis is now IMPLEMENTED. It is BUG-1445's guard, live, and it fired on BUG-1297 twenty minutes ago:

    ⚠ identical review findings recurred — escalated to advisor; not re-queued

That is the dependency being satisfied, observed, on the very spec the chain was built from.

SUGGESTED: repoint the BlockedBy from BUG-1476 to BUG-1445 and mark it satisfied, then dispose BUG-1476 as superseded. Yours to decide; I am flagging it because the ordering was written into both specs minutes ago and hardens the longer it sits.

ONE THING NOT TO LOSE IN THE SUPERSEDE, which I flagged earlier and matters more now that BUG-1495 depends on this guard's correctness:

    main:   pr_keyed_reviewer_verdict_arms_rework_guard      positive case
    #2029:  rework_guard_ignores_non_blocking_pr_verdict     NEGATIVE case, main has none

Main asserts a PR-keyed RequestChanges verdict ARMS the guard. Nothing asserts an APPROVED one does NOT. An implementation that armed on any verdict passes the current suite — and that is precisely the failure BUG-1495 describes, a guard firing against unchanged state when it should not. The negative test is worth cherry-picking onto main as a test-only change before #2029 is closed, and it is arguably part of BUG-1495's own acceptance rather than a salvage.
